companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
The input capacitor carries the switching current. Placed far away, or absent, the input rail carries it instead and the whole board sees the ripple.
The output capacitor turns the inductor's triangular current into a usable rail and closes the loop.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
The input capacitor carries the switching current. Placed far away, or absent, the input rail carries it instead and the whole board sees the ripple.
The output capacitor turns the inductor's triangular current into a usable rail and closes the loop.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
The input capacitor carries the switching current. Placed far away, or absent, the input rail carries it instead and the whole board sees the ripple.
The output capacitor turns the inductor's triangular current into a usable rail and closes the loop.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
The input capacitor carries the switching current. Placed far away, or absent, the input rail carries it instead and the whole board sees the ripple.
The output capacitor turns the inductor's triangular current into a usable rail and closes the loop.

rules.why: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
Two drivers on one net fight; whichever is stronger sources the other's short-circuit current.
An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.

An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
An open-drain pin can only pull down; without a pull-up its net never reaches a logic high.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.
VDD is specified for 3.0 V to 5.5 V; a rail outside that range either destroys the part or leaves it below its start-up threshold

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.

An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
An open-drain pin can only pull down; without a pull-up its net never reaches a logic high.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.

An FPGA runs several independent supplies — core, auxiliary, and one per I/O bank — and they are separate rails, not one rail arriving on several pins. base.ic's single bulk capacitor per device covers whichever rail it happens to sit on and leaves the others with only their decoupling, so this asks for one per supply net instead.
